goal: Help the developer make ClickOnce deploy the WebView2 loader needed by the installed WPF app.
must_include: Identifies the missing installed `WebView2Loader.dll` as the cause indicated by `DllNotFoundException`, not a `userDataFolder` permission problem.

Adds the WebView2 loader to ClickOnce publishing, for example a `PublishFile` item for `runtimes\win-x64\native\WebView2Loader.dll` with `TargetPath` set to `WebView2Loader.dll` and `PublishState` set to `Include`.
Considers the app's target architecture and includes the matching loader path (`win-x64`, `win-x86`, or `win-arm64`) rather than hard-coding the wrong architecture.
Notes that the WebView2 Runtime itself must still be present on client machines; including the loader DLL does not install the runtime.
must_not: Focuses on changing the WebView2 user data folder as the primary fix for this `DllNotFoundException`.
Copies the DLL manually on each client machine instead of fixing the ClickOnce publish manifest/project.
Includes only the design-time NuGet package reference and assumes ClickOnce will automatically install every native runtime file.
Tells them to rely on the Microsoft Edge browser executable instead of the WebView2 Runtime.
acceptable_alternatives: Use a post-publish target that adds the correct `WebView2Loader.dll` to the ClickOnce application files and manifest.
For supported project types, statically link the WebView2 loader with `WebView2LoaderPreference=Static` so a separate loader DLL is not required.
Use an MSIX/MSI installer that explicitly deploys both the app files and the WebView2 Runtime prerequisite.
solved: The answer changes the publish configuration so the correct architecture's `WebView2Loader.dll` is installed with ClickOnce and separately accounts for the WebView2 Runtime prerequisite.
partial: The answer says to include `WebView2Loader.dll` but omits ClickOnce project metadata or architecture/runtime considerations.
notes: The accepted answer used a `PublishFile` item and `WebView2LoaderPreference`; for managed WPF, grading should favor reliably including the correct native loader in the ClickOnce install.
